items.title: Iranian attack on Saudi tanker killed two Filipino sailors, Saudi Arabia says
items.description: The kingdom condemns the targeting of Sidr, which was reportedly hit by unknown projectiles in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday.

items.title: Protests in Spain over government's handling of Ceuta migrant crisis
items.description: Spanish opposition parties accuse Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez of abandoning the residents of Ceuta.

items.title: EU and Nato vow to step up pressure on Russia after 'new escalation' in Germany
items.description: Russia is accused of growing increasingly reckless after Berlin blamed Russia for a failed drone attack on Leipzig airport.

items.title: Rosenberg: Putin's veiled threat to UK part of Russia's campaign against West
items.description: The Russian president wants to keep Britain guessing - and stressing - over Moscow's real intentions.

items.title: Watch: Jury still unable to reach unanimous decision in Lindsay Clancy case
items.description: For a second time in two days, jurors told the judge they could not agree on a verdict in the murder trial.

items.title: Maltese tycoon acquitted of orchestrating murder of renowned journalist
items.description: Daphne Caruana Galizia exposed corruption and money laundering schemes in Malta before she was killed by a car bomb in 2017.

items.title: Netherlands moves billions in gold to London in 'crisis preparedness' move
items.description: The Dutch central bank removes some of its gold reserves from the US and Canada, saying it is because of "increasing geopolitical unrest".

items.title: Iran says US strike killed four at wedding in 'war crime' as US denies targeting civilians
items.description: Iranian media reports two children were among those killed when shrapnel hit a home. Iran then launched missiles and drones at US targets in the Middle East.

items.title: US sailors arrive in Thailand's Pattaya after record 250 days at sea
items.description: The USS Abraham Lincoln is docking close to Pattaya, known for its neon-lit nightlife, and for sex tourism.

items.title: Uber shuts operations in Nigeria and Uganda with immediate effect
items.description: Nigeria - Africa's most populous country - is proving a tough market for ride-hailing services.

items.title: Woman charged with juror intimidation in Lindsay Clancy trial
items.description: Dawn Light is accused of taking photos of jurors outside the Plymouth courthouse, a practice prohibited by the court.

items.title: Zelensky says airlines should avoid Russian airspace as Ukraine escalates drone operations
items.description: Chinese and Gulf state airlines are among those still using Russian airspace. Meanwhile, Russia says it will intensify its own attacks on Ukraine.
